mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% (GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth rate exceeds 2.0% in the last quarter but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate above 5.0% (FEDFUNDS) signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where PAYEMS increases by over 100k and UNRATE decreases by over 0.2pp, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 100 (INDPRO) indicates supply constraints that lead to inflationary pressures and reduced corporate capacity, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 100, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1300 thousand units (HOUST) signal a weakening housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST is below 1300, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation above 310 (CPIAUCSL) indicates persistent inflationary pressures that typically prompt aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL exceeds 310 but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate below 3.5% (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market that supports strong consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE is below 3.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 310) and elevated interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) signal a restrictive monetary policy environment that suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 310 and FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.
